boston-scientific-cyberattack.text: boston scientific says cyberattack could hit its 2026 outlook the marlborough-based medical-device maker said an august incident disrupted parts of its global operations and made its prior forecast harder to meet. boston scientific said tuesday that it is unlikely to meet previously issued third-quarter and full-year 2026 sales and adjusted-profit forecasts after a cyberattack disrupted global operations. reuters reported that the unauthorized activity was identified august 25 and caused network outages that affected manufacturing and order processing. the company said major distribution and manufacturing operations have resumed, while the full financial impact remains uncertain. the company had previously forecast 2026 adjusted earnings of $3.28 to $3.32 per share and sales growth of 5.5% to 6.5%. it plans to provide an updated outlook with third-quarter results in october. the incident is a reminder that cybersecurity risk can move quickly from an information-technology problem into a supply-chain and earnings issue for massachusetts manufacturers. new-england ma marlborough marlborough, ma massachusetts cybersecurity business healthcare

breaking-afghan-woman-first-terrorism-re.excerpt: The Justice Department used a court created in 1996 for the first time to remove a lawful permanent resident accused of helping conceal a terrorism plot.
breaking-afghan-woman-first-terrorism-re.text: u.s. deports afghan woman in first use of terrorism removal court the justice department used a court created in 1996 for the first time to remove a lawful permanent resident accused of helping conceal a terrorism plot. a 47-year-old afghan woman who held lawful permanent residency in the united states has been deported in the first case pursued through the alien terrorist removal court, reuters reported friday. the little-used court was created in 1996 to handle government efforts to remove people accused of terrorism-related activity. the justice department accused nazira haji zada of helping conceal a failed islamic state-inspired plan for a mass shooting on election day 2024. she was not criminally charged. her son and son-in-law pleaded guilty in related cases. proceedings in the special court can include classified evidence that the person facing removal is not permitted to review, a structure her public defender challenged on due-process grounds. haji zada agreed last month to end her challenge and consent to removal. chief judge joan ericksen approved the request, clearing the way for deportation. her attorney said the agreement should not be read as an endorsement of the court or its procedures. the case establishes a new precedent for a tribunal that had not previously been used in the three decades since congress created it, and it may draw further legal scrutiny. breaking breaking breaking / developing us united states immigration alien terrorist removal court justice department national security deportation

breaking-algeria-cuts-uae-diplomatic-tie.text: algeria cuts diplomatic ties with united arab emirates algiers cited unspecified hostile actions, while the uae said it hoped the rupture would be temporary. algeria severed diplomatic relations with the united arab emirates on thursday, an abrupt rupture between two arab governments whose ties had been strained for years. the algerian government cited what it called provocative and hostile actions but did not specify the conduct behind the decision. it said efforts to preserve the relationship had been exhausted. algerian media have previously accused the uae of trying to sow discord, adding to an increasingly public dispute. the uae responded that it hoped the break would be temporary and said it remained committed to relations based on shared interests. the statement left open the possibility of future diplomatic engagement but did not announce a mediation effort or timeline. ending formal relations can affect ambassadorial representation and routine government coordination, though neither side immediately detailed the practical measures that would follow. the lack of a specific allegation from algiers also leaves the immediate trigger unclear. further statements will determine whether the decision expands into broader restrictions or remains a diplomatic protest. breaking breaking breaking / developing international algiers algiers, algeria algeria united arab emirates diplomacy middle east

breaking-anak-krakatau-journalists-missi.excerpt: A speedboat carrying five photojournalists, two crew members and a guide lost contact while traveling to report on the Indonesian volcano.
breaking-anak-krakatau-journalists-missi.text: search underway for eight missing near anak krakatau a speedboat carrying five photojournalists, two crew members and a guide lost contact while traveling to report on the indonesian volcano. indonesian rescuers are searching the sunda strait for eight people whose speedboat lost contact while traveling to anak krakatau to cover volcanic activity. the group includes five photojournalists, two crew members and a route guide, the associated press reported. the boat departed carita in banten province, and relatives received its last known message at 6:13 p.m. monday saying the group had reached waters near the island. their last reported position was about 18.5 kilometers, or roughly 11.5 miles, from shore. search teams deployed tuesday had not established contact or confirmed the boat’s location by early wednesday. the journalists work for several indonesian and international news organizations, with one described as a freelance photographer. anak krakatau’s initial eruption ended sunday, but the volcano has continued intermittent activity involving explosions, lava and ash. officials had not established whether that activity, weather, mechanical failure or another cause was connected to the disappearance. the search remains active, and early details may change as rescue crews cover the area and review communications. more breaking breaking / developing international carita sunda strait, indonesia indonesia anak krakatau search and rescue journalists

breaking-bahamas-plane-family-found-dead.excerpt: Relatives located the victims after launching a search for the small plane, which lost contact while flying toward Miami.
breaking-bahamas-plane-family-found-dead.text: relative says four family members found dead after bahamas plane disappeared relatives located the victims after launching a search for the small plane, which lost contact while flying toward miami. four members of a family aboard a small plane that disappeared off the bahamas were found dead tuesday, a relative told the associated press. silvia larrieu said relatives searching by boat recovered the bodies and were working with the u.s. coast guard to bring them home. the victims were mario lamar, 80; his wife, lili lamar, 79; and their grandchildren, sofi sosa, 28, and christian sosa, 22. the pa-34 piper left great harbour cay in the berry islands on monday morning for miami executive airport. bahamas police said air traffic control lost contact when the aircraft was about 13 miles west of andros island. family members alerted authorities after messages went undelivered and the expected arrival time passed. the coast guard sent an aircraft to assist after bahamian authorities requested help, although poor weather delayed parts of the search. the developing work now centers on recovery and the investigation into what caused the plane to go down. authorities had not announced a cause in the information available tuesday night. more international bahamas bahamas plane crash u.s. coast guard aviation

breaking-bangladesh-measles-outbreak-100.excerpt: Authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases as disrupted immunization and vaccine shortages fuel a fast-moving public-health emergency.
breaking-bangladesh-measles-outbreak-100.text: bangladesh measles outbreak nears 1,000 deaths authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases as disrupted immunization and vaccine shortages fuel a fast-moving public-health emergency. bangladesh is battling what the u.s. centers for disease control and prevention lists as the world’s largest current measles outbreak, with 999 suspected and confirmed measles-related deaths reported since march, reuters reported wednesday. authorities have recorded more than 166,000 suspected cases. of those, 19,835 were laboratory confirmed, while more than 146,000 people were hospitalized. the outbreak has spread as routine immunization was disrupted during 2024 and 2025 and vaccine shortages left gaps in protection. an emergency measles-rubella campaign has reached more than 19.7 million children. health specialists say catch-up vaccination and restoration of routine immunization remain essential because a one-time campaign cannot fully repair missed doses or stop continued transmission. hospitals are also managing dengue cases, adding pressure to staff and beds. the death and case counts can change as records are reviewed, but the scale already shows how quickly measles can spread when vaccination coverage falls. measles is highly contagious, and outbreaks can become especially dangerous for young children and people with limited access to care. breaking breaking breaking / developing international dhaka bangladesh bangladesh measles vaccination public health

breaking-belgorod-drone-attacks-two-dead.excerpt: Regional authorities reported fatalities in Novy Oskol and Shebekino as attacks continued across Russia’s border region.
breaking-belgorod-drone-attacks-two-dead.text: two killed, seven injured in belgorod drone attacks, officials say regional authorities reported fatalities in novy oskol and shebekino as attacks continued across russia’s border region. two people were killed and seven were injured in drone attacks across russia’s belgorod region, regional authorities said thursday, in the latest reported violence along the border with ukraine. officials said one man died when a drone detonated at an unspecified facility in novy oskol. five people were reported injured in attacks across several other localities. in shebekino, another man was killed when a drone struck a car, while a woman traveling in the vehicle was injured. belgorod has been repeatedly targeted during the war because of its proximity to the ukrainian border. the initial report did not provide a complete account of property damage, identify all of the injured or establish whether military sites were among the targets. the casualty figures and circumstances were reported by russian regional authorities and could not be independently verified in the immediate account. responsibility was attributed to ukrainian drones by those officials. the situation remains developing, and later reports may revise the number of casualties or add details about the locations struck. breaking breaking breaking / developing russia belgorod belgorod region, russia belgorod russia ukraine drone attacks

breaking-borneo-haze-flights-forest-fire.text: thick haze disrupts flights on indonesia’s borneo island smoke from fires in west kalimantan disrupted flights for several days as thick haze reduced visibility and raised air-quality concerns. thick haze from fires disrupted flights for several days on indonesia’s portion of borneo, the associated press reported monday. visibility in parts of west kalimantan fell below one kilometer, creating problems for aircraft operations and worsening conditions for residents. the fires have burned for about a month during a prolonged dry period. more than 202,000 hectares were reported burned across indonesia from january through july, according to the ap report. smoke has also prompted school suspensions in other areas as officials monitor pollution levels. firefighters have been working to contain the outbreaks, with international support involved in the response. the flight disruptions and reduced visibility remained developing conditions, and authorities continued to assess where the smoke was thickest and how the fires were spreading. air travelers were advised to check with carriers because conditions can change quickly when smoke and visibility shift. officials continued to monitor the affected airports as the haze moved. breaking breaking breaking / developing west kalimantan west kalimantan, indonesia indonesia borneo west kalimantan forest fires

breaking-brics-adopts-new-delhi-declarat.excerpt: The 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict.
breaking-brics-adopts-new-delhi-declarat.text: brics unanimously adopts new delhi declaration on middle east war the 10-member bloc urged maximum restraint and peaceful dispute resolution despite sharp differences among members over the conflict. brics leaders unanimously adopted the new delhi declaration on saturday, expressing deep concern about the middle east war and calling for maximum restraint. the formal adoption converts an earlier agreement among negotiators into the 10-member group’s official summit position. the statement advocates a multilateral approach that respects national viewpoints and reiterates support for settling international disputes through dialogue, consultation and diplomacy. reaching consensus carried added significance because the expanded bloc includes both iran and the united arab emirates, a close u.s. partner, while the united states and iran have resumed exchanges of strikes after an august pause. the declaration also raised concern about unilateral tariff and non-tariff measures that distort trade, against a backdrop of u.s. sanctions on iran and russia. brics now includes brazil, russia, india, china, south africa, egypt, ethiopia, indonesia, iran and the uae. the declaration provides a common diplomatic text, but implementation will depend on whether members can translate broad calls for restraint into coordinated action. breaking breaking breaking / developing international new delhi new delhi, india brics new delhi middle east diplomacy

breaking-brics-joint-declaration-deal-20.excerpt: Negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it Saturday.
breaking-brics-joint-declaration-deal-20.text: brics reaches joint-declaration deal despite middle east divisions negotiators agreed on language that sources said would condemn unilateral aggression without naming a country, with leaders expected to consider it saturday. brics negotiators reached agreement on a joint declaration saturday as leaders began summit talks in new delhi, according to four sources familiar with the discussions. the reported deal is a significant test of the expanded group’s ability to maintain consensus while members iran and the united arab emirates remain divided over the gulf conflict. the sources said the draft was unlikely to name any country but would condemn unilateral aggression. leaders were expected to consider the document later saturday. india’s foreign ministry did not immediately comment on the reported agreement. host prime minister narendra modi opened the summit by urging members to turn their shared positions into concrete results and renewed his call for reform of the united nations security council. a brics foreign ministers’ meeting in may ended without a joint statement because members could not bridge their differences. the declaration therefore represents a diplomatic advance even before final approval. brics is also seeking greater influence over international financial and trade institutions. details may change as leaders debate and approve the final text. breaking breaking breaking / developing india new delhi new delhi, india brics new delhi summit india middle east diplomacy

breaking-brussels-airport-drone-traffic-.excerpt: Runway operations paused under a safety procedure that keeps traffic stopped until 30 minutes after the last sighting.
breaking-brussels-airport-drone-traffic-.text: drone sighting halts brussels airport traffic for about 30 minutes runway operations paused under a safety procedure that keeps traffic stopped until 30 minutes after the last sighting. air traffic at brussels airport was interrupted for about 30 minutes friday evening after a drone sighting, according to belgian air-traffic-control operator skeyes. runway operations resumed after the airport followed its established safety procedure for unauthorized aircraft near the airfield. the procedure pauses operations until 30 minutes after the most recent sighting, giving controllers and security authorities time to assess whether the airspace is clear. officials did not immediately disclose how many flights were delayed or diverted, and they released no details about the drone or its operator. the incident comes amid heightened concern in belgium over repeated unauthorized drone activity near airports and sensitive sites, including military facilities and a nuclear power plant. earlier episodes prompted the government to invest in counter-drone equipment. authorities have previously raised the possibility of foreign involvement in some sightings, but no evidence connecting friday’s event to any state or group was announced. although the immediate disruption ended, the lack of information about the drone leaves the security investigation open and underscores how even a short sighting can halt operations at a major international airport. breaking breaking breaking / developing belgium brussels brussels, belgium brussels airport drones aviation belgium

breaking-bukavu-school-fire-24-children-.excerpt: Officials said 19 girls and five boys were among the dead as flames also destroyed roughly 300 wooden homes in the rebel-held city.
breaking-bukavu-school-fire-24-children-.text: bukavu fire kills at least 24 children and destroys two schools officials said 19 girls and five boys were among the dead as flames also destroyed roughly 300 wooden homes in the rebel-held city. at least 24 children were killed when a fire tore through two schools and about 300 wooden homes in bukavu, a city in eastern democratic republic of congo controlled by afc/m23 rebels, a local official said thursday. the dead included 19 girls and five boys, according to south kivu’s vice governor in the rebel-appointed administration. twenty-nine people were reported injured, although accounts from hospitals and residents indicated that the toll could change as officials reconcile casualties. the fire was out by thursday afternoon, but smoke continued to rise from rubble and twisted roofing, a reuters witness reported. investigators had not determined the cause. bukavu has been under the control of the rwanda-backed afc/m23 movement since its rapid advance through eastern congo in 2025. that conflict complicates public administration and emergency response in a densely populated city. the immediate priorities are identifying victims, treating the injured, sheltering families whose homes were destroyed and establishing how flames spread into school buildings. officials and health workers cautioned that the death toll could rise, making this an active emergency with significant uncertainty around the final number of victims. breaking breaking breaking / developing international bukavu bukavu, democratic republic of congo bukavu school fire democratic republic of congo afc/m23

breaking-bulgaria-weapons-depot-explosio.excerpt: No injuries were reported after an overnight blast near Tsareva Livada, the second incident at a Bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks.
breaking-bulgaria-weapons-depot-explosio.text: explosion and fire spread through bulgarian weapons depot no injuries were reported after an overnight blast near tsareva livada, the second incident at a bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks. an explosion struck a weapons-storage site near tsareva livada in central bulgaria overnight, starting a fire that spread from one warehouse to another. authorities reported no injuries in the initial accounting. the incident is the second at a bulgarian munitions facility in recent weeks, adding urgency to the investigation while firefighters and security officials assess the site. bulgarian media identified the facility as being operated by emco, an arms-trading company associated with businessman emilian gebrev. the cause of the latest blast had not been established in the early reports. that uncertainty is significant because bulgaria has previously investigated a series of explosions at facilities storing ammunition intended for ukraine and georgia. in 2024, bulgarian authorities issued warrants for six russian nationals accused in older depot explosions between 2011 and 2020 and linked those cases to an attempted poisoning. moscow denied the allegations. there was no announced evidence connecting the tsareva livada blast to those cases, and the current fire remains a developing event. the immediate verified facts are the explosion, the warehouse-to-warehouse spread and the absence of reported injuries. breaking breaking breaking / developing bulgaria tsareva livada tsareva livada, bulgaria bulgaria weapons depot explosion fire emco

breaking-epa-power-plant-rule-repeal-202.text: epa moves to repeal power-plant climate rule, setting up court fights the agency says the rollback will cut industry costs, while environmental groups promise legal challenges and warn of broader pollution impacts. the environmental protection agency said monday it is repealing rules that limit greenhouse-gas emissions from coal- and natural-gas-fired power plants, the associated press reported. the agency also proposed a separate step that could prevent future administrations from regulating climate pollution from power plants. the repeal is expected to take effect after publication in the federal register, and environmental groups are preparing legal challenges. the epa said the rollback would save industry more than $300 billion in costs and give utilities more flexibility in deciding how to supply electricity. environmental and public-health groups said removing the limits could increase pollution and harm communities. the associated press reported that coal, gas and oil-fired power plants account for about one-quarter of the nation’s climate pollution. the epa’s separate proposal is expected to be finalized next year if it survives the rulemaking process. the announcements came as epa and other u.s. energy officials hosted a g20 ministerial meeting in houston. the changes represent a major shift in federal power-plant regulation and are likely to remain contested in court and in congress. breaking breaking breaking/developing dc washington washington, d.c. breaking epa power plants climate policy

breaking-first-circuit-usps-mail-ballot-.text: first circuit keeps block on new usps mail-ballot rule the boston-based appeals court declined to pause an injunction against federal requirements involving voter lists and ballot barcodes before the november election. a federal appeals court in boston declined thursday to let the u.s. postal service implement new mail-ballot requirements while litigation continues, leaving a lower-court injunction in place ahead of the november election. the rule would require states to provide lists of mail-ballot recipients and place unique barcodes on ballot envelopes. the postal service could refuse ballots that did not meet the requirements. a three-judge first circuit panel said election regulation belongs primarily to states and congress and cited the risk that voters could be disenfranchised if ballots were rejected. the justice department argued that the requirements were modest mail-processing regulations and asked the court to pause the injunction. the postal service has said it acted lawfully. states challenging the rule contend that the executive branch lacks authority to impose the conditions and that election systems cannot be reworked safely so close to voting. the administration has separately asked the supreme court to lift the injunction. thursday’s ruling does not resolve the underlying lawsuit; it determines which rules apply while the case proceeds. all 50 states permit mail voting in at least some circumstances. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states boston boston, ma first circuit usps mail ballots elections

breaking-gaza-hospital-generator-power-c.text: generator failures deepen power crisis at gaza hospitals engine-oil and spare-parts shortages are forcing medical facilities to ration generator power while aid groups warn that essential services are at risk. hospitals and displaced families in gaza are struggling to keep generators running as shortages of engine oil and replacement parts worsen an already severe electricity crisis. at nasser hospital in khan younis, one of four generators was out of service, reuters reported. staff were rotating power cuts to reduce the load on the remaining units, leaving patients who depend on ventilators, nebulizers and other powered equipment waiting for limited electricity. gaza has had no grid power since 2023, making generators central to hospitals, ambulances, water pumps and shelters. médecins sans frontières warned that dwindling oil and parts threaten those services. residents told reuters that privately generated electricity now costs about 20 times its earlier price, putting it beyond the reach of many families. israel’s cogat agency said a monitored mechanism facilitates the entry of equipment while seeking to prevent advanced items from reaching hamas and to ensure supplies reach civilians. aid groups say current access remains insufficient. with roughly two million people living largely in displacement sites, further generator failures could quickly interrupt medical and water services. breaking breaking breaking / developing gaza khan younis gaza strip gaza hospitals generators humanitarian crisis

breaking-houthis-hanish-islands-red-sea-.text: houthis claim control of two strategic red sea islands as yemen fighting widens houthi rebels say they seized greater and lesser hanish in the southern red sea, a claim that could signal a new front near the bab el-mandeb shipping route. houthi rebels in yemen said they had seized control of greater and lesser hanish, two islands in the southern red sea, as fighting in the region widened, the associated press reported monday. the islands sit near the bab el-mandeb strait, a passage connecting the red sea with the gulf of aden and an important route for commercial shipping. control of the territory could give the houthis a new position near maritime traffic, although the group’s claim was not independently verified in the report. saudi-backed forces were trying to retake territory, according to the ap. the report also linked the latest development to a broader escalation in yemen, where tens of thousands of people have been displaced since fighting intensified this month. the situation remains fluid, and the reported island seizure could not be confirmed by independent observers. any change in control or new restrictions near the strait could affect shipping risk assessments and add pressure to an already volatile regional conflict. breaking breaking breaking/developing yemen hanish islands, red sea breaking news yemen red sea

breaking-houthis-reach-perim-island-2026.text: houthis reach perim island at mouth of bab el-mandeb yemeni government forces withdrew from the strategic island as the group’s rapid red sea advance raised pressure on a vital shipping corridor. yemen’s iran-aligned houthis reached perim island in the bab el-mandeb strait on friday, according to four yemeni government sources cited by reuters. two sources said saudi-backed government forces had withdrawn from the island after the houthis also took the mainland town of dhubab, which faces it. perim sits at the mouth of a shipping lane connecting the red sea with the gulf of aden. control of the island could increase pressure on commercial traffic at a time when the strait of hormuz is already severely disrupted, forcing more attention onto the western route used by saudi energy shipments. the movement is a material extension of the houthis’ rapid coastal advance. yemeni government forces said they plan to deploy weapons and aircraft in an effort to retake captured areas and warned civilians to avoid a route between taiz and mocha. the houthis captured mocha and the hanish islands on thursday. the situation remains fluid, and control on the ground may change as government forces organize a counteroffensive. the immediate risk extends beyond yemen: any sustained disruption at bab el-mandeb could affect shipping schedules, insurance costs and energy supply routes linking asia, the middle east and europe. breaking breaking breaking / developing yemen perim island, yemen houthis perim island bab el-mandeb shipping

breaking-white-house-dpa-refinery-expans.text: white house weighs defense production act for refinery expansion officials are considering tools to improve and expand existing facilities, but reuters reports that no final decision has been made. the white house is considering whether to use the defense production act to expand u.s. oil-refining capacity as elevated fuel costs increase pressure on the domestic energy system, reuters reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. no final decision has been made, and further talks with refiners are expected. the discussions are focused on improving efficiency and adding capacity at existing facilities rather than relying only on the construction of entirely new refineries, which can take years and require large capital commitments. reuters reported that u.s. refining utilization has been running near 98%, leaving limited room to increase output through higher operating rates alone. the administration is also evaluating permitting changes, regulatory steps and investment incentives. the defense production act can give the federal government tools to prioritize contracts and support production considered important to national security, but any specific application to refining would depend on the policy ultimately selected. the review is developing against the backdrop of disrupted middle east energy flows and higher transportation costs. until an action is announced, the proposal remains one option under consideration rather than a new requirement for the industry. breaking breaking breaking / developing united states washington washington, d.c. defense production act oil refining white house energy fuel supply
